meta.note: Original recipes written for the meal generator. Metric units. 'pantry' = staples most kitchens have. 'difficulty' is 'easy' or 'medium'.

meals.name: Lemon garlic chicken traybake
meals.blurb: One tray, hardly any washing up. Everything roasts together.
ingredients: 4 chicken thighs, bone in, skin on
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Halve the potatoes and cut the onion into wedges.
Put the potatoes and onion in a large baking tray with 2 tbsp olive oil, a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix with your hands.
Place the chicken on top, skin side up. Rub with a little oil, salt and the herbs. Add the garlic cloves with their skins still on.
Cut the lemon in half. Squeeze one half over everything and put the other half in the tray.
Roast for 35-40 minutes, until the skin is golden and the juices run clear when you poke the thickest part. There should be no pink meat.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve.
meals.tip: Pat the chicken dry first for crispier skin.

meals.name: Chicken fajitas
meals.blurb: Sizzling strips of chicken and peppers in a warm wrap.
steps: Slice the chicken into thin strips. Slice the peppers and onion into strips too.
Toss the chicken with the seasoning and 1 tbsp oil.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken for 6-8 minutes, turning, until golden with no pink inside. Take a piece out and cut it open to check.
Add the peppers and onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Warm the wraps in the microwave for 20 seconds. Fill with the chicken mix, squeeze over some lime and add sour cream if you like.
meals.tip: Don't overcrowd the pan or the chicken will steam instead of browning.

meals.name: Creamy garlic chicken pasta
meals.blurb: A comforting pasta with a quick creamy sauce.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water for the time on the packet.
Meanwhile, dice the chicken into bite-size pieces. Fry in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 6-8 minutes until golden with no pink inside.
Crush in the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Crumble in the stock cube, add 100ml water and the cream. Simmer for 3 minutes, stirring.
Add the spinach (or peas) and stir until it wilts or heats through.
Drain the pasta, tip it into the pan, mix well and season to taste.
meals.tip: Save a splash of pasta water to loosen the sauce if it gets thick.

meals.name: Chicken stir-fry noodles
meals.blurb: Fast, flexible and uses a ready-made veg bag.
steps: Mix the soy sauce, honey and crushed garlic in a cup.
Slice the chicken into thin strips.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Cook the chicken for 5-6 minutes until golden with no pink inside.
Add the veg and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles and the sauce. Toss for 2-3 minutes until everything is hot and coated.
meals.tip: Cut chicken thin so it cooks through quickly.

meals.name: One-pot chicken and rice
meals.blurb: Everything cooks in one pan, so there's no juggling.
steps: Chop the onion. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan with a lid over medium heat. Fry the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the outside is white.
Stir in the rice and paprika. Crumble in the stock cube and pour in 400ml boiling water. Stir and bring to the boil.
Put the lid on and turn the heat to its lowest. Cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid.
Add the peas, put the lid back on and cook for 3 more minutes. Check that the rice is tender and the chicken has no pink.
Leave covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
meals.tip: If the pan looks dry before the rice is tender, add a splash of water.

meals.name: Spaghetti bolognese
meals.blurb: The classic. A big batch that reheats well.
steps: Finely chop the onion and grate the carrot, if using.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry the onion and carrot for 5 minutes.
Add the mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 8-10 minutes until it's brown all over with no pink left.
Crush in the garlic, add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, 200ml water, the crumbled stock cube and the herbs. Simmer with the lid off for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Cook the spaghetti following the packet. Drain, then serve with the sauce on top.
meals.tip: Leave out the carrot if you like, but it adds a little sweetness.

meals.name: Beef tacos
meals.blurb: Taco night with almost no effort.
steps: Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the mince and cook for about 8 minutes, breaking it up, until brown with no pink left.
Spoon off any extra fat. Stir in the seasoning and 4 tbsp water. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
Warm the taco shells following the packet.
Shred the lettuce and chop the tomatoes.
Fill the shells with beef, lettuce, tomato and cheese.
meals.tip: Set out toppings in bowls and let everyone build their own.

meals.name: Cottage pie
meals.blurb: Savoury beef under a golden mash topping. Worth the extra time.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into chunks. Boil in salted water for 15-20 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Meanwhile, chop the onion and dice the carrots. Fry in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes.
Add the mince and cook for 8-10 minutes until brown with no pink left.
Stir in the tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce, the crumbled stock cube and 250ml water. Simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas if using.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Drain the potatoes and mash with the butter, milk, salt and pepper.
Tip the mince into a baking dish. Spread the mash on top and rough it up with a fork.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
meals.tip: The fork ridges in the mash get crispy and golden.

meals.name: Easy chilli con carne
meals.blurb: A mild, hearty chilli that's easy to scale up.
steps: Chop the onion and pepper.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan. Fry the onion and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add the mince and cook for 8-10 minutes, breaking it up, until brown with no pink left.
Stir in the chilli powder, cumin and tomato puree for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and 100ml water. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Cook the rice following the packet and serve the chilli on top.
meals.tip: Start with less chilli powder. You can always add more.

meals.name: Homemade burgers
meals.blurb: Better than takeaway, and just mince and seasoning.
steps: Mix the mince with 1 tsp salt and some pepper using your hands. Don't squash it too much.
Divide into 4 and shape into flat patties about 2cm thick. Press a small dent into the middle of each.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the burgers for about 5 minutes per side until browned, with no pink in the middle and the juices running clear.
In the last minute, put a cheese slice on each and cover the pan with a lid or foil so it melts.
Toast the buns, then build your burgers with lettuce and tomato.
meals.tip: Don't press the burgers while they cook. It squeezes out the juices.

meals.name: Lemon baked salmon and greens
meals.blurb: Almost no prep, and hard to get wrong.
ingredients: rice, couscous or bread to serve
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Put the salmon and veg on a lined baking tray.
Drizzle with 1 tbsp olive oil and season with salt and pepper. Squeeze over half the lemon and lay slices of the other half on top of the salmon.
Bake for 12-15 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily with a fork.
Serve with rice, couscous or bread.
meals.tip: Cook until it flakes. Overcooked salmon turns dry.

meals.name: Honey soy salmon and rice
meals.blurb: Sticky, glossy salmon with a simple 3-ingredient sauce.
steps: Start the rice following the packet.
Mix the soy sauce, honey and crushed garlic in a shallow dish. Add the salmon and leave for 5 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat. Fry the salmon skin side down for 4 minutes, then flip and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Pour the leftover marinade into the pan and let it bubble for 1 minute until sticky. Don't skip the bubbling, as it makes the marinade safe to eat.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 4 minutes. Serve everything together.
meals.tip: Don't marinate longer than 15 minutes or the salmon gets too salty.

meals.name: Creamy lemon salmon pasta
meals.blurb: Fresh and creamy, with flaked salmon in every bite.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water following the packet. Add the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Season the salmon. Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat and fry skin side down for 4 minutes, then flip for 3-4 minutes. Flake into big chunks.
Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Return the pasta to the pot. Add the cream cheese, juice of half the lemon and 4 tbsp pasta water. Stir until creamy.
Gently fold in the salmon and serve.
meals.tip: Fold the salmon in gently so it stays in chunks.

meals.name: Salmon tacos
meals.blurb: Smoky salmon with a cool lime yoghurt sauce.
steps: Rub the salmon with the paprika, 1 tsp oil and a pinch of salt.
Fry in a pan over medium heat, skin side down, for 4 minutes. Flip and cook for 3-4 minutes until it flakes easily.
Mix the yoghurt with the juice of half the lime and a pinch of salt.
Shred the lettuce and warm the tortillas in the microwave for 20 seconds.
Flake the salmon into chunks and fill the tortillas. Add lettuce, avocado and a spoonful of sauce.
meals.tip: Skin crisps up nicely if the pan is hot before the fish goes in.

meals.name: Pesto salmon traybake
meals.blurb: Pesto does all the seasoning work.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan).
Halve the potatoes, toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and pepper on a baking tray, and roast for 20 minutes.
Take the tray out. Add the tomatoes and the salmon. Spread 1 tbsp pesto over each fillet.
Roast for another 12-15 minutes until the salmon flakes easily and the potatoes are tender.
meals.tip: Give the potatoes a head start since they need longer than the fish.

meals.name: Creamy scrambled eggs on toast
meals.blurb: Soft, silky eggs in minutes.
steps: Crack the eggs into a bowl with the milk and a pinch of salt. Whisk with a fork.
Put the bread in the toaster.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low-medium heat.
Pour in the eggs. Wait 20 seconds, then gently push them across the pan with a spatula.
Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look a little glossy. They keep cooking in the pan.
Spoon onto the toast and add pepper.
meals.tip: Low heat is the secret. Fast heat makes them rubbery.

meals.name: Cheese and veg omelette
meals.blurb: A filling meal that takes about as long as boiling a kettle.
ingredients: 1 handful of spinach, or 1/2 pepper diced
steps: Whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Heat 1 tsp butter in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook the veg for 2 minutes.
Pour in the eggs. As the edges set, pull them in gently and tilt the pan so runny egg flows out. Do this for about 1 minute.
When the top is mostly set but still slightly wet, sprinkle the cheese on one half.
Fold the other half over and slide onto a plate.
meals.tip: A non-stick pan makes the fold much easier.

meals.name: Egg fried rice
meals.blurb: The classic use for leftover rice.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add the peas and cook for 1 minute.
Push the peas to one side. Pour the beaten eggs into the empty space and stir for 1 minute until scrambled.
Add the rice and break up any lumps. Stir for 3-4 minutes until piping hot.
Add the soy sauce and the sliced spring onions. Stir and serve.
meals.tip: Use rice that was chilled quickly after cooking and eaten within a day.

meals.name: Shakshuka-style eggs
meals.blurb: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato sauce, perfect with bread.
steps: Chop the onion and pepper. Fry in 1 tbsp oil in a deep pan over medium heat for 6 minutes.
Crush in the garlic and add the paprika and cumin. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and simmer for 8 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Make 4 dips in the sauce with a spoon. Crack an egg into each.
Cover with a lid and cook for 5-7 minutes until the whites are fully set. The yolks can be runny or firm.
Serve straight from the pan with bread.
meals.tip: Cook the sauce until it's thick, or the eggs will slide around.

meals.name: Easy veg frittata
meals.blurb: A thick omelette you finish under the grill. Great hot or cold.
ingredients: 150g frozen veg (peas, sweetcorn) or leftover cooked veg
steps: Heat the grill to high. Use an oven-safe frying pan, with no plastic handle.
Fry the chopped onion in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the veg and cook for 2 minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt, pepper and half the cheese.
Pour the eggs into the pan. Cook over low heat for 6-8 minutes until the edges are set and the bottom is firm.
Sprinkle on the rest of the cheese and put the pan under the grill for 3-4 minutes until the top is set and golden.
Slide out and cut into wedges.
meals.tip: Keep the heat low so the bottom doesn't burn before the top sets.

meals.name: Crispy tofu stir-fry
meals.blurb: Golden, crunchy tofu in a simple soy and honey sauce.
steps: Start the rice following the packet.
Wrap the tofu in kitchen paper and press with a heavy pan for 10 minutes to remove water.
Cut into 2cm cubes. Toss with the cornflour and a pinch of salt.
Fry in 2 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning, until golden all over. Move to a plate.
Add the veg and crushed garlic to the pan for 3 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, honey and 2 tbsp water. Add to the pan with the tofu and toss for 1-2 minutes.
meals.tip: Pressing the tofu is what makes it crisp.

meals.name: Tofu scramble on toast
meals.blurb: An egg-free scramble that works for breakfast or dinner.
steps: Drain the tofu and crumble it into chunks with your hands.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the tofu and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add the turmeric, soy sauce and pepper. Stir for 2 minutes.
Add the spinach and stir until it wilts.
Serve on toast with sliced tomato.
meals.tip: Turmeric gives the yellow colour, so don't skip it.

meals.name: Easy tofu coconut curry
meals.blurb: Creamy curry from a jar of paste and a tin of coconut milk.
ingredients: 2 tbsp curry paste (mild korma or Thai)
steps: Start the rice following the packet. Cut the tofu into 2cm cubes.
Fry the tofu in 1 tbsp oil for 6-8 minutes until lightly golden. Move to a plate.
In the same pan, fry the chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add the curry paste and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the coconut milk and 100ml water. Simmer for 8 minutes.
Return the tofu and add the spinach. Cook for 2 minutes. Season to taste and serve with the rice.
meals.tip: Shake the coconut milk tin before opening so it mixes smoothly.

meals.name: Peanut noodles with tofu
meals.blurb: A fast peanut sauce you make with a spoon and a bowl.
steps: Cook the noodles following the packet.
Cut the tofu into cubes. Fry in 1 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden.
In a bowl, whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice and honey with 4 tbsp hot water until smooth.
Drain the noodles and toss with the sauce and tofu.
Top with sliced cucumber.
meals.tip: Add more hot water if the sauce is too thick.

meals.name: Sweet chilli baked tofu
meals.blurb: Hands-off baked tofu with a sticky glaze.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Press the tofu in kitchen paper under a heavy pan for 10 minutes.
Cut into 2cm cubes. Toss with 1 tbsp oil and the soy sauce. Spread on a lined baking tray.
Bake for 20 minutes, turning once halfway.
Toss in the sweet chilli sauce and bake for 5 more minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the rice following the packet and boil or steam the broccoli for 4 minutes. Serve together.
meals.tip: Space the cubes out so they crisp instead of steaming.

meals.name: Red lentil dal
meals.blurb: Cheap, filling and ready in half an hour.
steps: Rinse the lentils in a sieve under cold water.
Fry the chopped onion in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes. Crush in the garlic and add the curry powder. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, 700ml water and the crumbled stock cube. Bring to the boil, then turn down to a simmer.
Cook for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are soft and thick. Add a splash of water if it sticks.
Season with salt, stir well and serve with rice or naan.
meals.tip: Stir often near the end, because lentils stick to the bottom.

meals.name: Black bean quesadillas
meals.blurb: Crispy, cheesy and ready in about 15 minutes.
steps: Mash half the beans with a fork. Stir in the rest of the beans, the cumin and a pinch of salt.
Spread the bean mix over half of each wrap. Sprinkle with cheese and chopped spring onion, then fold in half.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Cook each quesadilla for 2-3 minutes per side until crisp and the cheese has melted.
Cut into triangles and serve.
meals.tip: Mashed beans act like glue to hold the filling in.

meals.name: Three-bean chilli
meals.blurb: A meat-free chilli from tins and a few spices.
steps: Chop the onion and pepper. Fry in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes.
Add the chilli powder, cumin and tomato puree. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and 100ml water. Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Cook the rice following the packet and serve the chilli on top.
meals.tip: Tastes even better the next day.

meals.name: Chickpea and spinach curry
meals.blurb: A fast tomato curry with the pantry basics.
steps: Fry the chopped onion in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes.
Add the curry paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas and 100ml water. Simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in the spinach for 2 minutes until it wilts. Season with salt.
Serve with rice or naan.
meals.tip: Mash a few chickpeas against the pan to thicken the sauce.

meals.name: Carrot and lentil soup
meals.blurb: A warming, thick soup from a handful of cheap ingredients.
steps: Chop the onion and carrots into small pieces.
Fry in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes. Stir in the cumin for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, 800ml water and the crumbled stock cube. Bring to the boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until the carrots are soft.
Blitz with a stick blender, or mash with a potato masher for a chunkier soup. Season to taste.
meals.tip: Serve with crusty bread for a full meal.

meals.name: Skyr berry breakfast bowl
meals.blurb: A high-protein breakfast you can put together in minutes.
steps: Spoon the skyr into a bowl.
Top with the oats or granola and the berries. If using frozen berries, microwave them for 30 seconds first so they soften.
Drizzle with honey and eat straight away.
meals.tip: Add a spoonful of peanut butter for extra staying power.

meals.name: Skyr overnight oats
meals.blurb: Make it tonight, eat it tomorrow. Needs 6+ hours in the fridge.
ingredients: 1 banana or a handful of berries
steps: Put the oats, skyr, milk and honey in a jar or container. Stir well.
Put the lid on and leave in the fridge for at least 6 hours, or overnight.
In the morning, stir it and add a splash of milk if it's too thick.
Top with sliced banana or berries.
meals.tip: It keeps for up to 2 days, so you can make two jars at once.

meals.name: Skyr pancakes
meals.blurb: Fluffy pancakes with extra protein from skyr.
steps: In a bowl, whisk the skyr, eggs and milk until mostly smooth.
Add the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt. Stir until just combined. A few lumps are fine.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat with a little butter or oil.
Pour in small ladlefuls of batter. Cook for 2-3 minutes until bubbles form on top and the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 1-2 minutes more. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
Serve with berries and honey.
meals.tip: Keep the heat low. The batter is thick and burns easily outside.

meals.name: Creamy lemon skyr pasta
meals.blurb: A light creamy pasta with no cream. Skyr gives the sauce body and protein.
steps: Boil the pasta in salted water following the packet. Add the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Mix the skyr, the zest and juice of half the lemon, the crushed garlic, parmesan, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Scoop out a mug of pasta water, then drain the pasta and peas.
Let the pasta cool for 1 minute. Add it to the bowl and stir, adding pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is smooth and creamy.
Add more lemon juice or pepper to taste and serve.
meals.tip: Never add skyr to a hot pan, because it splits. Mix it off the heat.

meals.name: Skyr tzatziki flatbreads
meals.blurb: Cool, garlicky tzatziki with crunchy veg in warm flatbreads.
steps: Grate the cucumber and squeeze out the water with your hands or kitchen paper.
Mix the cucumber with the skyr, crushed garlic, a squeeze of lemon, 1 tsp olive oil, salt and pepper. Add chopped mint or dill if you have it.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan or toaster for 1 minute.
Spread a thick layer of tzatziki on each flatbread. Top with halved tomatoes and salad leaves.
Fold or roll and eat.
meals.tip: Squeeze the cucumber well, or the tzatziki turns watery.
